title: Specialist - Commercial Standards Claims & Contract
description:
**Job Description**
**Specialist — Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts is a Business Analyst and SME on the Customer Operations Transformation programme.**
The outcome is a clear, governed set of commercial policies — credit, claims, pricing and trade terms — and customer agreements that are standard, compliant and correctly executed in the systems; fewer and cleaner customer claims; lower invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage; and <1 Day Resolution wherever the process allows: fewer claims arising in the first place, and faster, controlled settlement for those that remain. Everything this role does serves that outcome.
  
  
The scope spans Commercial Standards, Claims and Contracts end to end — formulation and governance of credit, claims, pricing and trade-terms policies, policy exceptions and delegation of authority, the customer agreement and contract lifecycle (drafting, approval, activation, amendment and renewal), pricing, rebate, discount and promotion setup, accruals, claims intake, validation and settlement, proof of performance, and the controls that link agreed terms to what is invoiced and paid. The role designs across this scope as one process rather than as separate contract, promotion and claims solutions. It works with market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service and Collections teams, GBO, D&T, the SAP and Control Tower (Claims and Deduction platform) teams and third-party vendors.
  
  
The role combines 5 capabilities in one person. As an SME, they formulate, document the global commercial policies — credit policy (credit limits, payment terms, risk categories, blocks and releases), claims policy (eligibility, evidence, time limits, approval and write-off thresholds), and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount and rebate guardrails, price-change control) — and the standards and controls that make them work in practice. As a business analyst, they interrogate contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data, document current and target process, and write requirements to standard. As a subject matter expert, they bring the functional depth to act as design authority for the fragment and to challenge solutions that would not work in the markets. As a sprint or project owner, they take a scope fragment through design, test and deployment on a two to four week value drop cadence. As a process and technology expert, they translate commercial policy, contract terms and controls into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction capability, and the contract and trade promotion management toolset.
  
  
**The defining discipline of this role is designing claims out at source, not processing them faster.**
A quicker claim approval is a smaller prize than a contract term clear enough never to be disputed; a faster settlement is a smaller prize than a promotion set up correctly in the system so the customer never needs to claim. The postholder is expected to use the data to find where in the commercial process claims are created — an ambiguous contract clause, a non-standard trade term, a late or incorrect pricing or promotion setup, an accrual gap, a weak approval control — and design the fix upstream into commercial policy, standards, contract templates, deal approval and master data, as well as into the claims and settlement design.
  
  
**Understanding of markets and of upstream and downstream impact is central to the role.**
A claim usually starts life as a commercial negotiation; a contract term becomes a pricing condition, an accrual, an invoice and, if anything is misaligned, a deduction in Collections. The postholder is expected to know what happens on either side of their own process — from deal negotiation through to cash and the P&L — and to design accordingly.
  
  
**This is a transformation design and delivery role, not an operational one.**
The postholder does not negotiate customer deals, draft or approve individual contracts, validate or settle individual claims, or manage customer relationships; that stays with market Commercial, Legal, GBO and BPO run teams. The role changes how that work is done — including the commercial policies, standards, contract templates, reason codes, analytics and controls that let run teams find and remove causes in BAU. The role formulates and recommends policy; final approval sits with the relevant policy owners and governance forums.
  
  
The role works independently within an agreed frame set by the workstream lead, gathers its own data, forms its own view and brings recommendations rather than questions. Where a Senior Specialist is assigned on the same fragment, it works under their design direction. Decisions are expected to be based on evidence rather than opinion, and every artefact is expected to meet the programme documentation, taxonomy and quality standards, including BPQMS.
  
  
**Analyse commercial terms, contracts and claims performance and baseline the problem — 25%.**
Document current-state credit, claims and pricing policies, commercial standards, contract lifecycle and claims processes across markets and identify variation from the global standard. Build the process, trade-terms and claim-type taxonomy and interrogate the data directly at portfolio level — customer agreements and terms, pricing and promotion conditions, accruals versus actuals, claims volume, value, ageing and rejection rates, invalid deductions, write-offs and trade-spend leakage — to baseline the problem per market and size the opportunity. Perform gap analysis between current process, commercial policy, contract terms, platform capability, controls and the target operating model, separating structural design issues from operational backlog. Support business-rule validation, master-data requirements and policy analysis. Aim for validated current-state documentation and a defensible baseline that will stand up to audit.
  
  
**Formulate commercial policies and standards, and design claims out at source — 25%.**
Support future-state design aligned to the global standard, always designing for the cause rather than the symptom. Formulate, document and maintain the global commercial policies the design depends on — credit policy (credit limits and risk categorisation, payment terms, credit blocks and release authority), claims policy (claim eligibility, evidence and proof-of-performance requirements, submission time limits, validation, approval and write-off thresholds) and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount, rebate and promotion guardrails, price-change control and margin protection) — with a clear policy-exception and delegation-of-authority framework, and take them through the governance forums for approval. Translate policy into the standards that operationalise it: standard trade-terms structures, contract and agreement templates, clause libraries, deal approval and delegation-of-authority rules, and the minimum data a contract must carry to be executed correctly in the systems. Use the baseline to show where claims are created — contract ambiguity, non-standard terms, pricing and promotion setup, accruals, proof of performance, master data — and design the fix upstream. Design the interventions: standard contract-to-condition setup, automated accruals and settlement, validated claim intake, reason-code frameworks and claims workflow. Prepare business requirements, functional specifications, process flows, business rules and user stories. Facilitate design workshops and document outcomes and decisions. Assess process, policy, financial and control impacts, and define how policy compliance will be monitored.
  
  
Deliver the outcome: standard contracts, fewer claims and <1 Day Resolution — 20%. Design for, and evidence, policy adoption and compliance across markets, an increase in contracts on standard terms and templates, fewer policy exceptions, a reduction in claims volume, aged claims, invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage, and movement toward <1 Day Resolution for appropriate claims and queries. Shape the build-out of SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction functionality, and contract and trade promotion management tooling as the primary levers on the outcome. Define the measures with the business owner, monitor post-go-live performance against the baseline, and recommend and, where owned, implement continuous improvements to the design. This is the accountability every other accountability serves.
  
  
**Own testing, deployment and adoption through the value drops — 20%.**
Translate requirements into working design on SAP, Control Tower and the contract and trade promotion management toolset with D&T, system integrators and vendors. Define and review test scenarios, support SIT and UAT, and manage defect resolution with business users. Break the work into fragments that can be delivered on the value drop cadence, and own the backlog, dependencies and risks for the fragment. Support deployment, hypercare and business readiness, and hand over up-to-date commercial standards, contract templates, process documentation, SOPs, controls and training materials to the run teams. Aim for SIT and UAT completed with minimal post-go-live defects and a clean handover into run.
  
  
**Manage delivery discipline and enable across the programme — 10%.**
Track requirements, risks, assumptions, dependencies and decisions throughout the lifecycle, and escalate early and precisely when the frame is wrong. Act as a trusted partner to market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service, GBO, D&T and vendors, and coach business users through testing, deployment and adoption. Enable the adjacent workstreams — Order-to-Invoice, Collections, Claims & Receivables, Customer Service and Supply — by surfacing cross-boundary impact before it becomes a deployment defect, and by handing design-level root causes to the workstream that owns them.
  
  

* Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts domain depth and business analysis, on a broad Customer Operations base. Real SME depth in commercial policy and customer contracts — credit policy and credit risk, claims policy, pricing governance, trade-terms structures, rebates, discounts and promotions, contract lifecycle management, accruals, and claims validation and settlement — sufficient to act as design authority and to write policy that is clear, enforceable and auditable, combined with strong business-analysis craft: process mapping, requirements gathering, gap analysis, functional-specification writing, user stories and workshop facilitation. Understands how claims and deductions are created across the commercial and Order to Cash process, and how contract wording, deal approval, pricing and promotion setup, master data and accruals drive them. Built on a general understanding of Customer Operations end-to-end (Order to Cash, Commercial and Supply) and of how markets actually work, including upstream and downstream impact. Knows Consumer Products industry standards and the realities of Beer, Wine & Spirits — distributor and wholesaler concentration, complex customer agreements, promotional and trade-spend claims, and route-to-market and regulatory constraints on trade terms. Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards.
* Data, technology and delivery discipline. Comfortable interrogating contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data directly, and translating requirements into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, the Control Tower claims and deduction platform, and the supporting contract and trade promotion management toolset. Understands the platform, the data model, the business rules, workflow and approval logic, and the operating model — retained, GBO and BPO — beneath the process. Strong on test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT), business readiness and hypercare, and on risk, issue and dependency management. Data-driven by instinct — baselines the problem, quantifies the opportunity and lets the evidence settle the argument. Able to prioritise across concurrent workstreams and deadlines.
* Design-for-prevention rigour, stakeholder influence and adaptability. Relentless about cause over symptom in design — not satisfied with automating a workaround when the claim could be designed out through a clearer standard, contract or setup. Strong stakeholder management and influencing across a global and local matrix, including senior Commercial, Finance and Legal stakeholders and policy governance forums, and consultative by default: frames the problem before prescribing and drives stakeholders toward aligned design decisions. Clear communicator, and able to manage conflict to a resolution rather than let it stall a decision. Comfortable being redeployed: arrives in an unfamiliar market or process, orients fast, and adds value quickly. Resilient, collaborative, and a visible role model for Diageo’s values.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in Finance, Business, Commercial, Law, Operations, IT or a related discipline.
* Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards. Business-analysis, Agile / Scrum or Lean Six Sigma credentials are an advantage; familiarity with SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower or similar claims and deduction platforms, or contract lifecycle or trade promotion management tools is a plus.

**Experience — Essential**

* Overall. 10+ years spanning transformation, business analysis and consultative experience, with a strong core of business analysis and SME design work in large-scale process transformation.
* Subject matter expertise. Deep functional understanding of credit, claims and pricing policy, commercial terms, customer contracts and agreements, trade promotions and claims within a Commercial and Order-to-Cash environment — someone who knows how claims and deductions are created by contract terms and commercial setup, and how standards and process should be designed to prevent them, not only the tooling. Operational exposure is useful context; the requirement is designing the process, not running it.
* Transformation. Experience in business process transformation, including current-state assessment and future-state operating model design, across the full lifecycle from design through testing, deployment and post-go-live stabilisation. Evidence of reducing claims, deductions, trade-spend leakage, cycle time or manual effort against a defensible baseline.
* Consultative. A track record of acting as a trusted business partner — framing the real problem, facilitating design decisions, aligning global and local stakeholders — and being measured on whether the business changed, not only on whether the deliverable shipped.
* Technology. Experience translating business requirements into functional specifications and solution design with D&T, system integrators and vendors, including test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT). SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower, or comparable contract, trade promotion or claims platform exposure is an advantage.
* Industry. FMCG or Consumer Products experience is essential. Beer, Wine & Spirits experience is strongly preferred.
* General understanding of Customer Operations end to end — OTC, Commercial and Supply — and of how markets actually operate, including upstream and downstream impact.

**Experience — Desirable**

* Experience formulating and governing commercial policy — credit, claims and pricing governance — and the standards beneath it: trade-terms frameworks, contract templates, clause libraries and deal approval policies — across multiple markets.
* Exposure to contract lifecycle management, trade promotion management, or claims and settlement automation, including AI-led claim validation and matching.
* Experience designing reason-code frameworks and claims analytics that let run teams identify and remove the causes of claims and deductions.
* Experience defining what must be global standard versus what requires market localisation.
* Experience working in a pooled, on-demand or competency-based delivery model across multiple workstreams.
* Prior experience of a GBO or shared services transition or operating model consolidation.

**About Us**
With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.

The organization promotes a growth-oriented work culture with the motto “Learn and Fun is the way to Earn,” supported by data-driven decision-making and a strict “No Safety No Work” policy that has resulted in a strong safety record. Extinct Fire Engineers invites both experienced candidates and freshers to join the ExtinctFire family and build long-term career prospects.
  
**Role Description**
The Articleship Company Secretary role is a full-time, on-site position based in Bengaluru. The role involves assisting in corporate secretarial functions, including preparing and maintaining statutory registers, drafting board and general meeting notices, agendas, and minutes, and supporting regulatory filings and documentation as per applicable company law and governance standards. The Articleship trainee will help in coordinating with internal departments and external stakeholders, compiling data and reports for compliance and audits, and maintaining accurate records for secretarial practices. The role also includes supporting internal process improvements, participating in knowledge-building activities, and contributing to the organization’s culture of safety, integrity, and continuous learning.
  
**Qualifications**
  

* Candidates should be pursuing or have completed Company Secretary (CS) professional or executive-level courses from a recognized institute.
* Should possess strong knowledge of corporate laws, company secretarial practices, and basic regulatory compliance requirements relevant to private limited companies.
* Should have skills in drafting, documentation, and record-keeping, with attention to detail and accuracy in preparing statutory registers, minutes, and official correspondence.
* Should demonstrate proficiency in MS Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and basic digital record management for maintaining secretarial and compliance data.
* Should possess effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and external professionals in a professional manner.
* Should demonstrate strong analytical, organizational, and time management abilities, along with a proactive and ethical approach to confidentiality and data integrity.
* Experience or exposure to industrial, manufacturing, or projects-based environments, especially in safety-focused organizations, will be an added advantage.

title: Commercial Compliance Manager, APAC
description:
**Bring more to life.**
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?
  
  
At Cytiva, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.
  
  
You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
  
  
Working at Cytiva means being at the forefront of providing new solutions to transform human health. Our incredible customers undertake life saving activities ranging from fundamental biological research to developing innovative vaccines, new medicines, and cell and gene therapies.
  
  
At Cytiva you will be able to continuously improve yourself and us – working on challenges that truly matter with people that care for each other, our customers, and their patients. Take your next step to an altogether life-changing career.
  
  
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
  
  
The
**Commercial Compliance Manager**
plays a pivotal role in protecting Cytiva's reputation and enabling sustainable growth by bringing our Commercial Compliance Program to life. Working closely with business and functional leaders, you will translate compliance expectations into practical, risk-based solutions, strengthen ethical decision-making, and use data, technology and AI to identify emerging risks and drive measurable improvement across our global commercial activities.
  
  
This position reports to the Senior Director, Compliance, Commercial and Operations and is part of the Legal and Compliance function. The role will be based on-site in Bangalore, India.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Channel Partner Compliance Management: Lead the effective implementation of policies and controls for third-party distributors. Partner with business leaders to assess, manage and monitor Channel Partner risk, resolve red flags, and ensure due diligence and approvals are completed in line with company requirements.
* Customer Interactions: Enable compliant and effective customer engagement by implementing relevant policies, advising stakeholders on higher-risk activities, supporting risk-based approvals, and meeting applicable local transparency reporting obligations.
* Auditing and Monitoring: Deliver risk-based auditing and monitoring activities, apply sound judgement and data-led analysis to selected transactions, identify root causes and emerging trends, and recommend proportionate corrective and preventive actions.
* Training and Communications: Create and deliver engaging, practical compliance training and communications for employees and third parties, including train-the-trainer sessions where appropriate, and assess whether learning is translating into changed behaviour.
* Systems, Data and AI Enablement: Support and continuously improve global Legal and Compliance systems, including user support, training and system maintenance. Use analytics, automation and approved AI tools to monitor adoption, identify potential non-compliance, improve workflow efficiency and generate actionable insights, while maintaining appropriate human oversight and protecting confidential information.

**Who You Are**

* BA/BS degree, or global equivalent, in Law, Finance, Information Technology, Business or a related discipline.
* Substantial experience designing, implementing or managing compliance, legal, regulatory, audit or risk programs, preferably in healthcare, life sciences or another regulated industry.
* Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English, with the confidence to influence stakeholders across cultures, functions and levels of seniority.
* Strong data and analytical capability, including building reliable data collection methods, using quantitative and qualitative analysis to assess compliance performance, identifying trends and translating insights into management action.
* Demonstrated ability to use AI and digital tools as part of daily work to improve the quality, speed and consistency of research, analysis, monitoring, communication and process execution, while applying appropriate judgement, validation and data protection controls. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the wider Microsoft 365 suite is also required.

**It Would Be a Plus If You Also Possess**

* Experience managing compliance programs in a regulated environment, including oversight of third-party distributors or other Channel Partners.
* Professional proficiency in an additional language relevant to the region, particularly Japanese or Korean.

Cytiva, a Danaher operating company, offers a broad array of comprehensive, competitive benefit programs that add value to our lives. Whether it’s a health care program or paid time off, our programs contribute to life beyond the job. Check out our benefits at Danaher Benefits Info.

For more information, visit www.danaher.com.

title: Company Secretary
description:
At Ball, integrity and trust are the foundation of who we are. Guided by our core values—"We Care. We Work. We Win.”—we create a culture where every voice matters and every idea drives progress.
  
  
Further your career at Ball, a world leader in manufacturing sustainable aluminium packaging. Achieve extraordinary things when you join our team, and make a difference in your professional development, the community, and around the globe!
  
  
Create a new future. Apply Today.
  
  
**Position Overview**
The Company Secretary (CS) is responsible for ensuring full compliance with statutory, legal, and regulatory requirements applicable to the organization. The role ensures effective corporate governance, supports the Board of Directors, manages secretarial records, ensures timely filings under the Companies Act, 2013 and related laws, and support corporate decision making.
  
  
The Company Secretary acts as a key link between the Board, senior management, regulators, auditors, and stakeholders. The role also oversees legal compliance, contract management, risk mitigation, and supports corporate initiatives such as mergers, expansions, and statutory audits.
  
  
Ensures that the company operates with the highest standards of governance, transparency, and ethical practices.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities Include**
**Corporate Governance & Board Management**

* Organize and document Board, Committee, and General Meetings as per Companies Act, 2013.
* Prepare agendas, notices, resolutions, and supporting papers.
* Maintain statutory registers and minutes (physical/electronic).
* Advise Board on governance, compliance, corporate responsibilities & secretarial practices.
* File statutory returns (AOC‑4, MGT‑7, DIR‑3 KYC, MSME, etc.) on time.

**Statutory & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with Companies Act, FEMA regulations, SEBI regulations (if applicable) etc
* Liaise with ROC, MCA, RBI, SEBI, and other regulators.
* Track legal changes and guide management on required actions.
* Manage CSR compliance, documentation, and committee support.

**Legal & Contract Management ( If Required )**

* Draft, review, and vet contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, and service/purchase agreements.
* Maintain contract repository and manage renewals.
* Support legal matters, disputes, arbitration, in consultation with the Legal team.

**Secretarial & Documentation Control**

* Maintain statutory registers (Members, Directors, Charges, Contracts, etc.).
* Manage share certificates, transfers, and related records.
* Handle loan/charge documentation and coordinate with banks.

**Risk Management & Internal Controls**

* Identify compliance risks and implement mitigation measures.
* Support internal, statutory, and secretarial audits.
* Develop compliance checklists, SOPs, and internal control systems.
* Based on the company’s framework of Compliance Calendar - follow-up with respective teams for the confirmation of compliance of the Applicable Laws.
* Managing the Internal Compliance tool of the Company & preparing the monthly compliance chart.
* Providing the Financial Impact assessment of Non-Compliance of other corporate Laws to the Board.
* Review of Organization Approval Matrix and assessing the implementation of the Matrix and its functionality.

**Stakeholder Management**

* Act as primary contact for shareholders, regulators, auditors, and authorities.
* Support investor relations (if applicable).
* Coordinate with Finance, HR, Operations, EHS, and Procurement Teams for organization-wide compliance.

**Corporate Strategy & Special Projects**

* Support M&A, JV, restructuring, and strategic initiatives.
* Draft policies, charters, and governance frameworks, in co-ordination with the Legal Team.
* Assist with expansion projects, plant registrations, and regulatory approvals.

**Other Responsibilities**

* Support insurance renewals and claims.
* Maintain confidentiality and be available during audits, inspections, and urgent compliance matters.

**What are we looking for?**

* Qualified Company Secretary (ACS / FCS) from ICSI.
* Law Degree (LLB).
* 6- 8 years of experience in secretarial and legal compliance roles in a manufacturing / engineering / industrial organization.
* Experience in handling Board meetings, statutory filings, and corporate governance.
* Exposure to contract management, legal documentation, and regulatory interactions.
* Experience in managing compliance for multi‑plant operations preferred.
* Strong knowledge of Companies Act, 2013, FEMA regulations, Labour Laws, and industrial regulations, and all applicable Corporate Laws.
* Legal and regulatory compliance expertise.
* Excellent drafting, documentation, and communication skills.
* High integrity, confidentiality, and ethical judgment.
* Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deadlines, and advice on corporate restructuring & governance.
* Proficiency in MCA portal, e‑filings, and MS Office.
* Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills.
* English (Proficient).
* Local language (preferred).

Ball Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We actively encourage applications from everybody, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, faith, ability, or orientation. Our products range from infinitely recyclable aluminium cans, cups to aerosol bottles solutions that enable our customers to contribute to a better world.
  
  
Each of us has a deep commitment to diversity and inclusion which is the foundation of our culture of belonging. Everyone at Ball is making a difference by doing what we love. Because what we create may change, but what we will always make is a difference.
  
  
Please note the advertised job title might vary from the job title on the contract due to local job title structure and global HR systems.

title: Manager - GDS Ethics Office
description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.
  
  
**Assistant Director – GDS Ethics Office**
This role is part of the GDS Ethics Function, and the individual will support the GDS Ethics team across all countries on areas related to ethics matters and sexual harassment investigations.
  
  
**The opportunity**
This is an exciting time to join the Global Delivery Services (GDS) ethics team as we scale up our program to match the expansion of the business. You will build your professional knowledge and credentials, learn how EY operates globally and work within a cross functional team of professionals to embed and improve the workplace culture by solving Ethics matters across its operating locations in India, Poland, China, the Philippines & Argentina.
  
  
As part of the role, you shall support the Ethics team and be part of the inquiries / investigations and ensure the compliance to the global code of conduct and other organizational processes and procedures.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities Require You To**

* Lead ethics team members and support the ethics officer in handling employee grievances and investigations related to workplace / sexual harassment, integrity issues etc. across various Geographies.
* Project / program management including the automation projects
* Lead the review, development and implementation of compliance processes, rules and standards as per the internal policies, automation projects etc.
* Review the investigation and reporting processes for any AI related opportunity implementation.
* Develop a thorough understanding of the governing policies of the Corporate and rules and regulations applicable to relevant geography.
* Support local business functions with Ethics related policy compliances.
* Learn technical aspects of various policy compliance requirements to help address Talent Team or employee queries
* Prepare case reports and ethics dashboards
* Support in other Risk Management projects or ethics team projects
* Work closely with Employee Relations team in managing and monitoring the cases and inquiries.
* Lead awareness sessions for managers and above ranks
* Detailed analysis of data, preparation of MIS and reports using tools / platforms such as excel.
* Work closely with Legal team in managing and monitoring the cases and inquiries.
* Stakeholder management and represent Ethics team in various internal forums.

**Skills And Attributes For Success**

* Experience of having worked as part of Ethics / ER / Risk management team at managerial level, with increasing scope of responsibilities.
* Ability to lead the teams across geographies.
* Anility to work in high pressure environment on time sensitive matters.
* Ability to learn ahead of the curve
* Working in multinational environment with different time zones
* High accuracy and on time delivery
* Attention to detail and process oriented, ability to analyse and cross check data points
* Automation experience will be an added advantage
* Good verbal and written communication skills
* Able to work in an unstructured & complex environment requiring out of box thinking, logical reasoning
* Able to continuously add value to assigned processes and develop solutions
* Ability to learn and understand the EY’s global policies as well as familiarity with other Risk Management initiatives outside of area of expertise
* Ability to manage tasks and activities in a timely manner and be responsible for specific outcomes
* Basic knowledge of project management tools and methodologies
* Ability to keep confidential sensitive information
* Strong research and communications skills
* Ability to successfully handle multiple tasks
* Interest in working with a culturally diverse team from around the globe to design, develop, and deploy programs and share knowledge
* Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills, with an inclusive approach
* Effective communicator with good written and oral presentation skills
* Team player and active listener with the ability to respond to and develop the ideas of others
* Experience working in an international setting and resolving cross border issues
* Ability to keep confidential sensitive information

**To qualify for the role, you must have**

* Bachelor’s / postgraduate’s Degree in Commerce, Finance, Arts, Law or HR.
* Advanced MS office knowledge (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
* Exposure to lead projects and prepare required MIS / dashboards
* 8-10 years’ experience in Operations/HR/People Functions, preferably corporate compliance areas with minimum of 5-6 years of experience in Team Lead role.
* Dealt / handled inquiries / investigations and understanding of basic aspects of running an inquiry with an ability to draft investigation reports
* Experience related to handling investigations
* Experience in handling workplace grievances – workplace harassment / sexual harassment / Ethics complaints / financial frauds / forensic investigations
* Understanding of compliance needs
* Previous experience of having supported on ethics matters

**Ideally, you should also have**

* An eye for efficiency and process improvements
* Planning skills and ability to prioritize the workload
* Attention to details and sense of ownership
* Ability to stretch in the busy period for high quality and on time delivery
* Ability to operate and flex in an ambiguous and changing environment to respond to emerging priorities
* Experience of working to deadlines and delivering high quality outputs
* Ability and willingness to periodically work flexibly e.g., participating in calls outside of standard office hours (early morning/late night) to support our global organization

**What We Look For**

* Working in a team of experts with deep domain knowledge
* Opportunity to work in fast paced multinational environment
* Positive attitude and dependable team player
* Ability to deal with problems in a practical and common-sense way, proactively applying judgment when required.
* A high standard of Excel and PowerPoint skills
* Flexibility to adapt activities based on the team priorities
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, producing work of a high quality that meets business demands
* Able to establish credibility, respect and trust in their working relationships and internal networks, particularly with the members of the Risk and Ethics Network

**What We Offer**
EY Global Delivery Services (GDS) is a dynamic and truly global delivery network. We work across six locations – Argentina, China, India, the Philippines, Poland and the UK – and with teams from all EY service lines, geographies and sectors, playing a vital role in the delivery of the EY growth strategy. From accountants to coders to advisory consultants, we offer a wide variety of fulfilling career opportunities that span all business disciplines. In GDS, you will collaborate with EY teams on exciting projects and work with well-known brands from across the globe. We’ll introduce you to an ever-expanding ecosystem of people, learning, skills and insights that will stay with you throughout your career.
  
  

* Continuous learning: You’ll develop the mindset and skills to navigate whatever comes next.
* Success as defined by you: We’ll provide the tools and flexibility, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.
* Transformative leadership: We’ll give you the insights, coaching and confidence to be the leader the world needs.
* Diverse and inclusive culture: You’ll be embraced for who you are and empowered to use your voice to help others find theirs.

**EY | Building a better working world**
EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.
  
  
Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.
  
  
Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

title: Paralegal
description:
**About Alaan**

Alaan is an AI-native finance platform for businesses in the Middle East. The platform combines corporate cards, expense management, cross-border payments, accounting automation, treasury, business banking\*, and more, with AI doing the work finance teams used to do by hand: coding transactions, chasing approvals and receipts, flagging policy breaches, placing treasury deposits, and closing the books.

Our mission is to simplify finance for businesses so they can save time and money.

Over 3,000 businesses use Alaan, from first-time founders to enterprises like Careem, G42, Tabby, Al Barari, and Rivoli. Since 2022, they have saved more than 2.2 million hours of manual finance work.

Alaan has raised $55Mn to date, including one of the largest Series A rounds in Middle East history, backed by Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India), Y Combinator, 468 Capital, and 885 Capital, among others. Headquartered in Dubai, Alaan has more than 250 employees across its Dubai, Riyadh, and Bangalore offices, with a team that comes from Careem, McKinsey, BCG, Goldman Sachs, Amazon, Revolut, Rippling, and the world’s leading firms.

Alaan has been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 list, UAE Future 100 list, selected as an Endeavor company, and ranked the No. 1 spend management platform in EMEA by G2.

\*Alaan is a fintech company, not a bank. Business bank accounts are issued by ruya.

**About the role**

We’re looking for a hands-on
**Paralegal**
to support the day-to-day legal operations of Alaan’s B2B fintech business across the GCC.

You will support the Legal team across commercial, corporate, regulatory and legal operations matters. The role will manage assigned workflows and administrative processes; substantive legal analysis, non-standard drafting, negotiations and final approvals will remain with the appropriate member of the Legal team.

This is a strong opportunity for a commercially minded lawyer who wants broad exposure, high ownership, and a clear path to growth in a fintech environment.

**What you'll do**

**Contract Administration and Matter Support**

* Manage the intake and administrative triage of legal requests, ensuring that instructions and supporting documents are complete before routing matters according to agreed priorities and timelines.
* Prepare initial drafts of routine documents using approved templates and playbooks, including NDAs, order forms, addenda, vendor agreements and customer documents.
* Conduct initial completeness and consistency checks, identify deviations from approved templates or playbooks, and refer those deviations to the Legal team for review.
* Coordinate internal approvals, signatures, filing and distribution, while maintaining a complete record of the request, relevant approvals and final executed documents.
* Monitor renewal dates, expiry dates, notice periods and contractual follow-up actions, and notify the Legal team of upcoming deadlines.

**Legal Operations and Knowledge Management**

* Maintain the legal review register, contract repository, vendor and matter trackers, corporate calendar and other legal records, ensuring that information remains complete, accurate and current.
* Apply consistent naming, filing, version-control and access standards across legal documents and repositories.
* Support the maintenance of approved templates, playbooks, checklists and precedent libraries under the Legal team’s direction.
* Assist with legal workflow automation and approved AI-enabled processes, including conducting initial quality checks and ensuring that outputs requiring legal judgement are referred for review.
* Compile status reports covering open matters, responsible stakeholders, deadlines, blockers, ageing and required follow-up actions.

**Corporate and Regulatory Support**

* Assist with entity maintenance and the preparation and organisation of corporate records, board and shareholder documents, powers of attorney, licences, KYC packages and required filings.
* Support regulatory submissions, licence maintenance, audits and due diligence exercises by collecting, checking, organising and tracking supporting information and evidence.
* Maintain checklists and calendars for corporate, regulatory and filing requirements, and notify the Legal team of upcoming deadlines or missing information.
* Conduct targeted legal and regulatory research under the Legal team’s direction and prepare concise summaries identifying the relevant sources and key findings for review.

**Cross Functional and Administrative Support**

* Coordinate with internal stakeholders to obtain complete instructions, approvals and supporting materials required by the Legal team.
* Communicate applicable legal processes, documentation requirements and matter status using approved guidance, while referring substantive or non-standard legal questions to the appropriate lawyer.
* Follow up proactively on outstanding actions and deadlines, and promptly alert the Legal team to identified gaps, delays or potential risks.
* Support legal and project meetings by preparing relevant materials, recording action items and monitoring their completion.
* Handle confidential, personal and commercially sensitive information in accordance with applicable policies and access requirements.

**What we're looking for**

* A bachelor's degree in law or a recognized paralegal or legal studies qualification. Admission as a lawyer is not required.
* 1 to 2 years of experience as a paralegal, legal operations professional, contract administrator or in a similar role within a law firm or in-house legal team.
* Practical experience supporting signature workflows, trackers, repositories and corporate records.
* Excellent organization and attention to detail, with a strong record of closing loops and meeting deadlines.
* Clear written and verbal English and the ability to summarize information concisely.
* Confidence using Word, Excel or Google Workspace, e-signature tools and document or contract management systems.
* Sound judgment on what can be handled through an approved process and what must be escalated.
* Comfort working across multiple jurisdictions and priorities in a fast-moving environment, including collaboration during UAE business hours.

**What's in it for you**

* Contribute to building the Middle East’s most beloved fintech brand from the ground up
* Benefit from a role with significant ownership and accountability
* Thrive in a flexible hybrid culture with ample work-life balance
* Participate in exciting offsite events
* Competitive salary and equity
* Enjoy additional perks like travel allowances, gym memberships, and more

title: US Paralegal Specialist
description:
**Role Summary**
This role provides paralegal-level corporate and litigation support for FME's US legal matters from the GBS India Legal Center of Excellence in Bangalore, handling matter administration, entity/compliance administration, contract execution support and litigation support tasks under the direction of US-based attorneys.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
***Matter & Case Administration***

* Post documents to the legal tracker and other matter-management systems
* Open new cases/matters and set up corresponding legal tracker records
* Support onboarding of outside counsel
* Support vendor setup for settlement payments

***Corporate Entity & Compliance Support***

* Liaise with registered agents on entity filings
* Assist in responding to know-your-customer (KYC) inquiries from banks and financial institutions
* Maintain the annual US attorney registration/licensing verification list
* Procure apostilles for cross-border document legalization
* Maintain the legal tracker
* Liaise with the Philippines-based accounts payable team on legal billing matters
* Perform general administrative assistant responsibilities in support of the legal team

***Contract Execution Support***

* Create redlines and comparisons of contracts to support attorney review
* Route contracts for internal approvals and signatures, and obtain signatures for contract execution
* Upload documents to virtual data rooms ("clean rooms") to support due diligence and transaction processes

***Litigation Support***

* Coordinate settlement payments
* Monitor the damages tracking spreadsheet and track monetary recoveries
* Set up, maintain and release legal holds; update legal referrals internally
* Support responses to subpoenas involving FME employees (where FME is not a party), under attorney direction

**Level-Specific Scope**

* Performs the tasks above independently with limited supervision from supervising attorneys and the Paralegal Manager; may begin to review and guide administrative/entry-level colleagues on routine instances of this work
* Makes decisions on moderately complex to complex coordination, drafting and administrative matters, often requiring judgment about process and prioritization; escalates matters requiring legal interpretation, litigation strategy, or transaction terms to supervising attorneys
* Contributions begin to influence team-level process improvements (e.g. legal tracker usage, workflow standardization) but do not set functional strategy
* Represents FME in routine coordination with external parties (registered agents, banks on KYC matters, document-legalization services) within a clearly defined, attorney-authorized scope
* Modifies existing administrative and coordination processes to improve efficiency; does not set new firm-wide policy independently

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree required (law degree not required); paralegal certificate or equivalent qualification preferred
* Bachelor's degree with approximately 3-6 years of relevant experience, including experience in corporate and/or litigation paralegal support, ideally supporting US legal matters from an LPO, GCC/GBS, or in-house legal environment
* Familiarity with US corporate entity administration (registered agents, KYC/banking compliance, attorney licensing tracking) and litigation support processes (legal holds, subpoena response, settlement tracking) is a plus
* Experience with legal matter-management/tracker systems, contract redlining/comparison tools, and virtual data room platforms preferred
* Strong organizational skills and high attention to detail; ability to manage multiple concurrent administrative and coordination workstreams
* Excellent written and spoken English required
* Discretion and ability to handle confidential corporate and litigation-related information

title: Operational Risk, Senior Associate
description:
Role Summary
  
  
State Street uses third parties to support internal processes and the delivery of products and services to clients. These relationships are evaluated and risk-assessed through the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Program.
  
  
The Third-Party Risk Management Associate will support the effective execution of activities across one or more TPRM lifecycle pillars. Depending on business requirements, the role may include reviewing TPRM cases and engagement records, reviewing and challenging inherent risk assessments, coordinating supplier due diligence outreach, monitoring and reviewing due diligence submissions, preparing executive summaries, and managing relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  
  
The successful candidate will apply sound risk judgement, identify and resolve data or process inconsistencies, maintain complete and accurate records, and communicate TPRM requirements and assessment outcomes clearly. The role requires close collaboration with Engagement Managers, third-party suppliers, risk-domain subject matter experts, Business Advisors, Procurement, Legal, and TPRM teams to support timely, consistent, policy-aligned, and audit-ready outcomes.
  
  
**Job Duties And Responsibilities**

* Develop and maintain a strong understanding of State Street’s business lines, products and services, third-party operating model, and TPRM lifecycle requirements.
* Review and evaluate TPRM SNOW cases, Archer engagement records, assessment records, and supporting documentation for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and compliance with applicable policies, standards and procedures
* Manage assigned case queues, review and effectively challenge TPRM cases and support business lines in faster onboarding of third-party suppliers.
* Identify inconsistencies or gaps in inherent risk questionnaire responses and work with Engagement Managers and relevant stakeholders to resolve issues before approval.
* Apply knowledge of inherent risk questionnaire logic, scoring, question interdependencies, and due diligence triggers to confirm that the resulting inherent risk rating and due diligence requirements are appropriate.
* Prepare and distribute due diligence questionnaires and supporting requirements to third-party suppliers or internal service providers within established timelines.
* Monitor due diligence progress, perform follow-ups and escalations, and maintain clear records of outreach, responses, decisions, and outstanding actions.
* Perform completeness and quality reviews of returned due diligence questionnaires and supporting artifacts before routing the assessment to the appropriate risk-domain subject matter experts.
* Coordinate follow-up questions, clarification discussions, and supplier meetings; track responses and facilitate resolution of outstanding items.
* Review and analyse due diligence results, assessment conclusions, control-effectiveness ratings, and identified findings to confirm that outcomes are sufficiently supported and accurately documented.
* Prepare clear, concise, and audit-ready executive summaries that communicate the engagement scope, inherent risk profile, due diligence results, control effectiveness, findings, residual concerns, and required acknowledgement or next steps.
* Coordinate executive-summary review and issuance with Engagement Managers, Executive Sponsors, Business Advisors, risk-domain subject matter experts, and other relevant stakeholders.
* Build and maintain effective working relationships with third-party suppliers, Engagement Managers, business stakeholders, Procurement, Legal, risk-domain subject matter experts, and TPRM partner teams.
* Explain TPRM requirements, risk-analysis conclusions, findings, and remediation expectations clearly and professionally, and guide stakeholders toward timely resolution.
* Ensure that TPRM decisions, approvals, exceptions, and supporting evidence are accurately captured in Archer and relevant repositories to support governance, audit, and regulatory review.
* Support the preparation of management information, metrics, trend analysis, and status reporting for TPRM leadership and governance forums.
* Maintain and enhance procedures, checklists, templates, job aids, frequently asked questions, and other process documentation.
* Identify opportunities to improve process efficiency, data quality, control effectiveness, stakeholder experience, and consistency of TPRM outcomes.
* Participate in system testing, process-change initiatives, remediation programmes, quality-assurance reviews, audits, and regulatory inspections.
* Maintain flexibility to work across TPRM pillars and support emerging programme priorities arising from business, regulatory, policy, technology, or operating-model changes.
* Perform all responsibilities in accordance with State Street’s risk appetite, policies, standards, ethical requirements, and control expectations.

**Skills**

* Strong knowledge of third-party risk management principles, lifecycle activities, and governance requirements within a regulated financial-services environment.
* Sound risk judgement and the ability to assess the reasonableness, completeness, and consistency of information and supporting evidence.
* Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to identify gaps, challenge assumptions, and develop practical resolution paths.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Strong stakeholder and relationship-management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes while maintaining professional and constructive working relationships.
* Ability to manage multiple cases, competing priorities, and tight deadlines in a high-volume, control-focused environment.
* Strong organisational, documentation, and time-management skills, with close attention to detail.
* Strong customer-centric mindset and commitment to providing clear guidance and responsive support to business and supplier stakeholders.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and related reporting tools.
* Working knowledge of Archer or a comparable governance, risk, and compliance platform is preferred.
* High ethical standards, professional integrity, and commitment to maintaining appropriate confidentiality.

**Qualifications**

* Overall professional experience of 2 or more years, preferably within banking, financial services, risk management, compliance, procurement, audit, controls, or a related field.
* Relevant experience in Third-Party Risk Management, operational risk, supplier risk, vendor management, due diligence, or another risk-and-control function.
* Practical experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred: TPRM case review, inherent risk assessment, due diligence outreach and completeness review, risk assessment coordination, findings management, executive-summary preparation, or stakeholder relationship management.
* General knowledge of third-party risk domains, including Operational Resiliency, Operational Risk, Cybersecurity, Information Sensitivity and Access, Privacy, Physical Security, Reputational Risk, Compliance, Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Bribery and Corruption, Financial Viability, and Tax Evasion.
* Experience working with internal stakeholders, third-party suppliers, and subject matter experts in a matrixed and globally distributed organization.
* Experience preparing management reporting, governance materials, executive communications, audit evidence, or regulatory-response documentation is preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in business or a postgraduate management qualification is preferred.
* Relevant professional certification such as CRVPM, CRISC, CISM, CISA, CBCI, or an equivalent risk-management qualification is advantageous.
* Prior experience with Archer or a comparable governance, risk, and compliance platform is preferred.
* Please note: The role is required to support internal clients during the first half of US working hours.

**About State Street**
Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
  
  
We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
  
  
As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Strong stakeholder and relationship-management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes while maintaining professional and constructive working relationships.
* Ability to manage multiple cases, competing priorities, and tight deadlines in a high-volume, control-focused environment.
* Strong organizational, documentation, and time-management skills, with close attention to detail.
* Strong customer-centric mindset and commitment to providing clear guidance and responsive support to business and supplier stakeholders.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and related reporting tools.
* Working knowledge of Archer or a comparable governance, risk, and compliance platform is preferred.
* High ethical standards, professional integrity, and commitment to maintaining appropriate confidentiality.

**Qualifications**

* Overall professional experience of 7 or more years, preferably within banking, financial services, risk management, compliance, procurement, audit, controls, or a related field.
* Relevant experience in Third-Party Risk Management, operational risk, supplier risk, vendor management, due diligence, or another risk-and-control function.
* Practical experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred: TPRM case review, inherent risk assessment, due diligence outreach and completeness review, risk assessment coordination, findings management, executive-summary preparation, or stakeholder relationship management.

title: Healthcare Community Contracting Sr Associate
description:
Amgen’s Research and Development (R&D) Business Operations organization addresses complex business challenges with outstanding people, tools, and processes. The team delivers on key initiatives and capabilities to support R&D. This position is primarily responsible for overseeing and processing healthcare compliance related contracting and payments of proposed arrangements by Amgen staff with Members of the U.S. and global Healthcare Community (i.e. Fee for Service, Scientific Exchange, Consulting, Sponsorship, Donation, Exhibits, Advisory Boards or other similar engagements). We are looking for talent who have play a key role in supporting the healthcare contracting process and ensuring accurate and timely payments to members of the health care community. The senior associate requires a solid understanding of contracting as well as SAP software and its functionalities. The senior associate will collaborate with global, cross-functional teams, including legal, sourcing, accounts payable, and finance, to ensure smooth and seamless contract management and payment operations. We are a team that delivers for our partners!
  
  
Required Competencies and Skills:
  
  
Key Responsibilities:
  
  
Prepare, process and coordinate standard agreements and amendments using approved templates and established contracting procedures; identify and escalate non-standard terms, exceptions and complex matters for members of the healthcare community (Fee for Service, Consulting, Sponsorship, Membership, Donation, Exhibits or other similar engagements). Maintain contract documentation and ensure compliance with contractual terms and conditions. Coordinate end-to-end contract execution, including onboarding, maintenance actions, and distribution. Maintain trackers, status fields, agreements, invoices, forms, expense documentation and supporting materials in the approved system of record. Triage intake from Amgen R&D or other supported functions to appropriate contract managers, as needed. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with sourcing, accounts payable, and other relevant teams to streamline financial processes and resolve any issues or discrepancies. Produce routine reports and data pulls on FFS hours, contract status, aging, payment status, engagement history and documentation completion. Ensure effective communication and foster positive working relationships. Process invoices, reimbursements, and payments related to healthcare contracts. Verify accuracy of invoices and resolve discrepancies with suppliers and providers. Ensure timely payments and adherence to payment terms. Ensure compliance with internal controls, policies, and regulations. Develop and enforce policies and procedures related to contracting and payment operations. Demonstrated ability to execute defined processes accurately, maintain documentation quality and meet service-level expectations in a high-volume environment. Participate in audits and assist with compliance-related activities as required. Contribute to the development and implementation of strategic initiatives to optimize contracting and payment processes.
  
  
Knowledge:
  
  

* Excellent computer and MS Office skills
* Excellent writing skills; detail-oriented
* Communicates effectively within and outside department
* Familiarity with SAP
* Working knowledge of standard contracting and payment workflows, supplier onboarding, data-entry standards and applicable enterprise systems.
* Knowledge of current and legally binding contractual language and terminology.
* Solid understanding of purchasing and supply chain procedures.
* Solid understanding of standard operating procedures (SOPs) and healthcare regulations.
* Solid understanding of standard contracting legal principles.

Problem Solving:
  
  

* Ability to process simple transactions from end to end, engaging business partners where appropriate.
* Identify and escalate business issues needing resolution, as well as identifying potential process improvements and manage multiple assignments at one time.
* Identify missing information, validate submission completeness and recognize discrepancies or out-of-process requests.
* Review and either approve payments or triage errors to the appropriate Amgen staff member.
* Review invoice/expenses related to Fee for Service Arrangements (i.e. CARFs) and triage any issues.
* Review invoice/expenses related to Advisory Board Arrangements (i.e. ABCARFs) and triage any issues.
* Communicate and escalate contractual and/or payment challenges to leadership team.
* Exercises good judgment.
* Interact with business partners to ensure compliance processes and standards are understood and followed.

Contribution:
  
  

* Consistent with Amgen’s Healthcare Compliance Policy and Standard Operating Procedures:
* Review proposed arrangements via Amgen’s healthcare compliance operations system of record (C3).
* Support Amgen staff members with any related questions and/or concerns such as C3 system support,
* Ability to read legal documents and facilitate legal review, interpret financial reports and technical documents.
* Manage payment inquiries that are received via the HCC Payment Requests mailbox from RAEs, Service Providers etc. Outcome may include further reviews, research and/or triage.
* Communicate clearly and professionally with internal stakeholders and external participants to obtain information, confirm next steps and support process completion.
* Proofread, edit and fact-check legal documents for accuracy and consistency.
* Time management and problem-solving skills.
* Other duties as assigned.

Master's or Bachelor's degree and 5 - 8 years of related resource management, paralegal, contracting and/or financial accounting experience.

Familiarity with biopharmaceutical industry as well as medical and scientific terminology. Knowledge of advocacy functionality at a large biotechnology organization.
  
  
Working understanding of healthcare regulations, contract terms, and payment processes.

The Legal Counsel will be responsible for providing end-to-end legal support to the Bank across corporate, commercial, lending, regulatory, and dispute matters. **Responsibilities**
**KPIs**
**Strategy and Planning**

* The counsel is expected to partner closely with business, risk, compliance, credit, and operations teams to facilitate transactions while safeguarding the Bank’s interests.

Early-stage involvement to advise on optimal deal structures (secured/unsecured, syndicated, bilateral, escrow, guarantees).
  
  
Align the transaction structure with the bank’s risk appetite, regulatory conditions, and security enforceability.
  
  

* Develop standardized templates for facility agreements, security documents, pledge deeds, mortgages, and inter‑creditor arrangements to reduce TAT.
* Interpret RBI Master Directions, circulars, KYC/AML rules, Embed legal safeguards into product features in relation to setting up/launching of new products or structuring any deals including drafting/vetting and negotiating all contracts, agreements and other documentation.
* While negotiating with third parties/lawyers orsettling non standard documents/client documents for new products ensure that the interest of the Bank is protected from a legal perspective
* Map critical cases in DRT, NCLT, High Courts, consumer forums, arbitrations, criminal complaints.
* Prioritize high-value exposures, reputationally sensitive matters, and systemic risks.
* Ensure meeting up with TAT as a single contributory or that of a team

**Advisory ,Policies, Processes & Procedures**

* Helping business lines and function structure transactions, products, contracts, set up procedures along best practices, negotiate arrangements and legal terms with third parties, resolve legal problems, and propose and advise on solutions that help the business lines complete their transactions/resolve issues within the bank’s operational/legal framework.
* Assist the General Counsel/Corporate Legal Head /seniors in compliance with Bank legal policies and assist in setting up, where necessary, relevant local legal policies and procedures to reflect specific legal requirements of India.
* Ensure that all transaction/Document is in consonance with Applicable Law and/or Policies and Process as stipulated by the Bank.
* Any policy renewals for other stakeholders/LRM to be reviewed, updated and adhered to
* Advise on substantive legal issues and questions of law.
* Provide legal advice and support as required generally by business teams and other functions like human resources, finance, compliance etc.
* Advise and support businesses in relation to the structuring, negotiation and execution of third-party agreements entered into by relevant legal entities within India
* Develop standard agreements and templates together with legal guidelines for products and documentation as appropriate and keep such documentation and guidelines updated.

**Stakeholder Management**
**In Consultation With Team Leads And Seniors**

* Highlight the consequences and liabilities to the stakeholders/management so as to ensure that calculated calls are taken
* Primary responsibility will be to provide support and legal advice to Large Corporates/Wholesale Banking/Structured deals/Trade Finance/Transaction Banking Products/Recovery Teams/IBU etc
* Provide legal advice and support and transaction management services for all Bank business activities.
* Provide general advise to the Bank branches, subsidiaries and affiliates, as required, on legal issues arising from the organization and management of the relevant legal entities within India including corporate structure governance and operations.
* Regular coordination and joint meetings with stakeholders to ensure that any teething issues are resolved.

* Develop a balanced and calculated approach in arriving at solutions keeping in mind the larger interests of the Bank

* Monitor trends in the regulatory and statutory environment for their impact on an organization and suggest an action plan for addressing them.
* Keeping abreast with latest legal developments.
* Monitor legal developments which may affect the businesses especially bank business operations and provide appropriate legal advice and support in relation to such issues.

* Endeavour to prepare/draft documents or address legal issues in house without any dependence on external counsels or law firms.
* Ability to draft bespoke documents/communications/Policies, Processes etc.

**Dispute Resolution and Litigation**

* Manage Disputes, Co-ordination and follow-up with outside legal counsels and drafting of Complaints, Replies, Misc Applications, Affidavits etc. in Civil as well as Criminal litigation matters including Recovery of debts.
* Any letters/correspondences/complaints/ litigations where a reply/written statement to be sent/filed should be promptly completed within the requite timelines to avoid any escalation /penal consequences to the Bank.

To assist in innovations within the Bank and ensure that processes are built around bringing efficiencies. Ideate and implement digitization ,smart documents and time saving techniques wherever possible

As part of MSCI's AI Contract Team, you'll work closely with Commercial Legal teams across the Americas, EMEA and APAC, negotiating technology and data agreements and helping embed AI tools into how the team works. The environment is fast paced but collegial, built on close working relationships within Commercial Contracts and with other functional departments at MSCI.

No programming experience is necessary, but you should show self-directed adoption of new technology, tools you've taught yourself, processes you've changed or workarounds you've built, and ideally use of AI tools on live legal work.

Strong project management skills, with the organisational capability to manage multiple deals and projects in a fast paced environment.
  
  
Experience negotiating complex technology and IP transactions.
  
  
An entrepreneurial, can do spirit and a proactive desire to quickly learn the business and rapidly come up to speed in new areas.
  
  
A positive, execution oriented outlook, with superior listening skills, drafting ability and attention to detail.
  
  
Strong communication skills and the ability to build and maintain strong relationships with clients and colleagues.
  
  
A law degree and licence to practise.

description:
NY Equity Documentation Group , Vice President, Institutional Equity Division
  
  
This role is in Mumbai and requires working with the NY Equity Documentation Group based in New York. The role will require a fast-learning, dynamic, pro-active, and self-motivated person to assist the team in its day-to-day activities.
  
  
The current opening is for a professional within the NY team based in Mumbai, with responsibility for documentation aspects of OTC derivative transactions, prime brokerage, cash and stock-lending transactions in the NY region.
  
  
Institutional Securities Documentation (ISD) is a global team based in several locations (including New York, London, Hong Kong, and Tokyo). The NY equity documentation group is part of global ISD and is comprised of a group of negotiators with legal backgrounds (i.e. practicing lawyers in HK/UK/NY; and/or as holders of law degrees/master’s in law). Within the NY IED we are part of the risk function and we support the equity businesses and handle documentation for prime brokerage and listed derivatives, over-the-counter on equity swaps/options (vanilla and exotic) on global equity underlying, stock-lending, warrants issuance, cash trading, equity research, regulatory remediation and subsets of documentation relating to our coverage areas.
  
  
From global institutions to hedge funds, investors come to Morgan Stanley for sales, trading, and market-making services in almost every type of financial instrument in all the world’s financial markets. Morgan Stanley professionals use our network and technology to provide liquidity and sophisticated analysis, to manage risk and execute reliably in the fast-changing markets.
  
  
Morgan Stanley’s Institutional Equity Division (IED) is a world leader in the origination, distribution and trading of equity, equity-linked and equity-derivative securities. Our broad and deep client relationships, market-leading platform and intellectual insights enable us to be a world-class service provider to our clients for their financing, market access and portfolio management needs.
  
  
Global Markets Group is the offshoring arm of Morgan Stanley’s Sales & Trading businesses in India. It covers functions across IED, associated to sales, trading, analytics, strats, risk management and documentation.
  
  
**What You'll Do In The Role**

* Manage the team of lawyers on the ground, co-ordinate with stakeholder on team dynamics, work management and allocations. Grooming/ training of team
* Draft, negotiate and execute (including amendments to) master derivatives agreements, including but not limited to ISDA, VM CSA, IM CSA, equity swaps /options and prime brokerage related documentation.
* Review and analyze constitutional documents of the client, to establish their capacity and authority capabilities for entering derivative transactions with Morgan Stanley.
* Review and analyze capacity and authority legal opinion from external counsel and highlight issues to Risk and Legal for approvals where applicable.
* Work closely with MS internal stakeholders, to obtain approvals on deviated terms identified in negotiable agreements, with clear implication on deviated terms to enable internal stakeholders to make informed decisions.
* Handle business unit’s queries on the terms of documentation ISD handles.
* Participate in globally or locally led projects related to documentation requirements.
* Undertake tasks directly related to the coordination and lifecycle management of the clients’ agreements and act as the primary point of contact for the clients for all tasks originating from the NY region.
* Responsible for administering and facilitating the agreement execution process; maintain and update clients’ contract database/systems; attend to day-to-day coordination among internal procurement and legal teams with respect to such contracts; and perform due diligence to ensure contract terms and conditions as well as information of the parties is reflected in the client’s contract database/systems.

**What You'll Bring To The Role**

* Law graduate with relevant 13+ years of experience in financing/derivatives is preferred.
* Experience in team management will be preferred.
* In-house documentation negotiation experience or paralegal experience in corporate law firm is preferred.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills. Prepared to speak to clients (internal and external) at all times.
* Proficiency in English is a must. Good team player with potential to lead a team.
* Solid quantitative skills and strong interest in business, economics, and law.
* Willingness and ability to provide quality service to the Firm's clients and to promote and enhance the Firm franchise.
* Willingness to work in dynamic environment and the ability to excel under pressure.
* Proficiency and interest in technology and systems development.
* Organized, pro-active, ability to multi-task and work efficiently, detail-oriented, and self-sufficient.

**What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley**
At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

DiaLawGue has an exclusive mandate from a full-service law firm with offices across India to hire an Senior Associate for its General Corporate & Advisory practice. The role is based in the firm's New Delhi office, full-time and in office. The firm advises businesses, investors, institutions and individuals across corporate, commercial and disputes work. It is a client-focused firm that puts its clients' needs first, and it looks for people who take ownership of their work and act without waiting to be asked.

**At a glance**

Joining: Immediate
